question: What is the primary goal of diagnostic investigations in the intensive care unit?

options.A: Guiding immediate interventions for unstable patients
options.B: Reducing overall hospital stay duration below three days

explanation: Critical care diagnostics focus on rapidly identifying physiological changes to drive immediate, life-saving therapeutic decisions. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why must clinicians carefully weigh the timing of diagnostic tests for critically ill patients?

options.A: Diagnostic machines cannot function in high-humidity environments
options.B: Moving or disturbing an unstable patient carries physiological risks
options.C: Unstable patients require conscious sedation for every blood test
options.D: Laboratory reagents are strictly rationed in intensive care units

explanation: Transporting or manipulating a critically unstable patient for diagnostics can precipitate hemodynamic collapse, requiring careful risk-benefit analysis. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: Where is the physical reference point for levelling an arterial line pressure transducer?

options.A: Phlebostatic axis at the fourth intercostal space
options.B: Umbuticus along the midline of the abdomen
options.C: Xiphoid process of the inferior sternum
options.D: Suprasternal notch at the base of the neck

explanation: The transducer must align with the phlebostatic axis to accurately reflect true central venous and arterial pressures. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of performing an Allen test before radial artery cannulation?

options.A: Identifying systemic coagulation disorders prior to minor surgery
options.B: Checking collateral ulnar blood flow to protect hand tissue perfusion
options.C: Determining the optimal angle for needle insertion into the skin
options.D: Measuring baseline systemic blood pressure without electronic monitors

explanation: The Allen test ensures the ulnar artery can adequately supply the hand if radial artery thrombosis or occlusion occurs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which parameter on an arterial blood gas report primarily reflects the respiratory component of acid-base balance?
explanation: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide reflects how effectively the lungs are eliminating or retaining carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient with severe metabolic acidosis will typically show which compensatory laboratory finding?

options.A: Elevated bicarbonate and increased PaCO2 via hypoventilation
options.B: Normal bicarbonate and severely elevated arterial oxygen tension
options.C: Unchanged pH with doubled serum potassium and sodium levels
options.D: Decreased bicarbonate and reduced PaCO2 via hyperventilation

explanation: Metabolic acidosis features low bicarbonate, prompting the respiratory system to blow off carbon dioxide to compensate. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: Serum lactate is primarily monitored in critical care as an indicator of which condition?

options.A: Acute bone marrow depression from drugs

explanation: Anaerobic metabolism resulting from inadequate tissue oxygen delivery leads to a buildup of lactic acid in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are cardiac troponins frequently measured in intensive care units for patients without primary cardiac complaints?

options.A: Systemic stress and sepsis can cause myocardial injury without classic chest pain
options.B: Troponins universally rise whenever any peripheral limb is infected
options.C: Laboratory protocols require cardiac markers for every patient receiving oxygen
options.D: High troponin levels confirm that the patient has normal kidney function

explanation: Critically ill patients often experience type 2 myocardial infarction or myocardial depression due to severe systemic inflammation and stress. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the FAST exam in trauma and critical care?

options.D: Detecting free fluid in body cavities

explanation: The FAST scan is a rapid bedside ultrasound tool designed to identify intraperitoneal, pericardial, or pleural hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h5)

question: A nurse cares for a hypotensive trauma patient whose bedside ultrasound reveals a collapsed, hyperdynamic inferior vena cava. What does this finding most likely suggest?

options.A: Severe fluid overload requiring emergency diuresis
options.B: Cardiac tamponade compressing the right atrium
options.C: Normal physiological response to rest and sleep
options.D: Fluid responsiveness and intravascular volume depletion

explanation: A small, collapsible inferior vena cava indicates low central venous pressure and a likely positive response to fluid administration. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which imaging modality is most commonly used at the bedside daily to confirm endotracheal tube placement?
explanation: Portable chest X-rays are performed frequently at the bedside to verify line and tube positions without moving the patient out of the ICU. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a major safety consideration when transferring a mechanically ventilated patient for a CT scan?

options.A: Absolute prohibition against using battery power on monitors
options.B: Unavoidable permanent loss of mechanical ventilator calibration
options.C: Immediate requirement for surgical tracheostomy prior to leaving
options.D: Risk of accidental device dislodgement and physiological instability

explanation: Intrahospital transport of critically ill patients carries high risks of line dislodgement, ventilator disconnection, and acute deterioration. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) in an unresponsive critically ill patient?
explanation: Many critically ill patients experience hidden seizure activity that is only detectable via continuous electrical brain monitoring. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Cerebral perfusion pressure is calculated using mean arterial pressure and which other critical parameter?
explanation: Cerebral perfusion pressure equals mean arterial pressure minus intracranial pressure, representing the net pressure driving blood flow to the brain. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which nursing action is essential immediately following an invasive diagnostic procedure at the bedside?

options.B: Discharging the patient back to the general medical ward
options.C: Reassessing baseline vital signs and inspecting the access site
options.D: Discarding all monitoring equipment without documenting data

explanation: Post-procedure assessment is critical to catch early complications such as hemorrhage, hematoma, or acute hemodynamic instability. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is strict aseptic technique vital when nurses assist with critical care diagnostic line insertions?

options.A: Compromised skin barriers increase the risk of severe catheter-related bloodstream infections
options.B: Diagnostic sensors will short-circuit if exposed to any biological moisture
options.C: Sterility prevents the patient from feeling any discomfort during insertion
options.D: Hospital accreditation standards prohibit documenting unsterile procedures

explanation: Critically ill patients are highly immunocompromised, making strict infection control mandatory to prevent life-threatening sepsis from invasive lines. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h8)
